title: Who's Who: Tobias Rooke
summary: Lens grinder and experimentalist whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Tobias Rooke (1725–1791) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a lens grinder and experimentalist whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

A master of inexpensive instruments, Rooke assembled the matched plates used in the paired-shadow assays of 1738 as an apprentice and later improved their repeatability. He marked every lens by its flaws, making it possible to rule out defects that had once been mistaken for discoveries.
His surviving workshop ledger is coveted as much for its failures as its successes.

For Alderwick readers, Tobias Rooke is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
